findings.title: Merged initialState is a new object on every render, so Renderer may apply the saved filters again over the user's choice.
findings.body: `{ ...savedState, ...initialState }` builds a new object each time `renderContent` runs. Before this change, `initialState` was the app's own stable reference. `useLastResults` says that "`Renderer` applies an `initialState` that changes later too, over what the user chose, and runs the queries again". If `Renderer` detects that change by reference, here is the failure: the dashboard reopens with a saved state, the user picks another filter, and the root re-renders for some other reason (`isFetching`/`isLoading` toggles, a title update, the `refreshing` flip). The Content slot calls `render()` again, gets a fresh object, and puts the dashboard back on the saved filter, re-running the queries. No test changes a filter after a restore and then re-renders. I could not see `Renderer`'s comparison, so this is not confirmed. Fix: keep the merged object stable, for example by caching it in a ref keyed on `savedState` and `initialState`, or by memoizing it in `ArtifactRendererRoot` and passing the merged value.

held.title: The restored state is checked against the version only once and is still passed after the version on screen changes.
held.body: `restoredRef` is reset only when `[reads, id]` change, and the version check runs only when it is first set. Trigger: a dashboard opened on v1 restores its saved v1 state, then a new version (v2) streams in while the content stays shown. `savedState` (the v1 state) keeps going to `Renderer` as `initialState` for the v2 program, which contradicts "a state for the version on screen". A remount through `rendererKey` would apply it to v2. Fix: store the version in `restoredRef` and return `savedState` only while it matches `requestRef.current.version`.
